title: The martyrs of Libya (15 February)
hook: Coptic Christians killed on a beach in Libya, now honored in the Roman Martyrology

segments.voice: Yesterday, Cyril and his brother Methodius, who built an alphabet so a people could hear the Gospel in their own tongue. Your line was love and letters. Who got a note from you? Day nine hundred sixty-eight.

The saints of the last few days lived long ago, in stories handed down. Today's saints were workers, in our own time. Men who had left their villages in Egypt to find jobs in Libya, to send money home to their families. They were kidnapped by an armed group, dressed in orange, led onto a beach by the sea, and killed. Their killers filmed it and sent the film around the world. Reports of the film say that, at the end, some of the men were heard calling on Jesus. The Church remembers them as the martyrs of Libya, and has a short name for them too.
screen: `WORKERS FAR FROM HOME.` → `A BEACH, AND A FILM.` → `CALLING ON JESUS.`

segments.voice: The men were, almost all of them, Coptic Orthodox Christians, from the ancient Church of Egypt. One man who died with them was from Ghana, and tradition among the Copts holds that he chose to stand with the others. Here's what makes this day unusual in a Catholic calendar. The Coptic Orthodox Church is not in full communion with Rome. They have their own pope in Alexandria, their own liturgy, their own saints. Their pope declared these men martyrs and saints of his Church. Later, Pope Francis received the Coptic pope at the Vatican and announced that the men would be added to the Roman Martyrology, the Catholic Church's official list of saints and martyrs. A Church honoring martyrs who were not its own members, because of how they died. Pope Francis had a phrase for this: an ecumenism of blood. Those who kill Christians, he said in effect, do not stop to ask which church they belong to. Catholics and Copts still differ on real questions, and both say so. But in the Martyrology, the names stand together. In the Greek of the Acts of the Apostles, the word for witnesses is the word English borrowed as martyr. In the Douay-Rheims, Jesus tells his followers, "you shall be witnesses unto me," and he sends that witness out to the uttermost part of the earth. A beach in Libya is one of those far places. These men did not preach a sermon there. Their witness was a name on their lips.
screen: `COPTIC CHRISTIANS FROM EGYPT.` · `A CHURCH NOT IN FULL COMMUNION WITH ROME.` · `ADDED TO THE ROMAN MARTYROLOGY.` · `AN ECUMENISM OF BLOOD.` · then, large: `YOU SHALL BE WITNESSES UNTO ME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for, or remember, Coptic Christians. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the families in those villages, who sent their sons out to work and waited for money and calls that stopped coming. Then widen it: Coptic Christians today, in Egypt and in cities all over the world, getting up for church, raising children, burying their dead. If you pray, you can hold them before God in your own words, or with the Lord's Prayer. If you don't, simply hold them in mind, one breath for the families, one for the men. The bell holds the time.
The martyrs of Libya. Coptic Christians killed on a Libyan beach, declared saints by their own Church and added to the Catholic Martyrology.
Your line: the twenty-one. Today, learn one thing about a church or a faith other than your own, and keep it with respect. Day nine hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: The Coptic Orthodox Church keeps these men as martyrs and saints on 15 February, and since their inclusion in the Roman Martyrology Catholics also remember them that day, often praying for Christians who suffer for their faith.
